$comment: Policy for the AL-Go issue triage agent. This file is policy; the workflow and orchestrator are mechanism. JSON rather than YAML so it can be read without adding a PowerShell YAML dependency to every job.

engine.$comment: Guardrails anchored on the production issue-triage agent in microsoft/PowerToys, adjusted for Copilot CLI: --max-ai-credits has a documented floor of 30, so PowerToys' value of 10 (a gh-aw frontmatter setting, a different mechanism) is not valid here. 30 credits is roughly $0.30 per run.

publish.$comment: allowedLabels is a security boundary, not a convenience. The publish job intersects the agent's suggested_labels with this list, so anything unexpected is dropped rather than trusted. blockedLabels is evaluated first. Both reuse AL-Go's existing label vocabulary - see labels.json for why no new labels are introduced.
publish.$removeTriggerLabelComment: Borrowed from the retired github/ai-assessment-comment-labeler, which did this well: removing the trigger label after a run makes re-triage idempotent - add the label again to re-run, rather than having to remove and re-add it. Only done when actually publishing; in dryRun and shadow the label is left alone, because a label silently vanishing with no comment would be baffling.

safety.$criticalPathsComment: Checked mechanically against traced_locations at publish time. If a traced file matches, fix_risk is forced to critical regardless of what the model concluded - the model missing that Github-Helper.psm1 is shared surface is exactly the mistake this is here to catch. Prefix match, repository-relative, forward slashes.
safety.$evidenceComment: A HIGH-confidence area or a definite fix_risk with no traced location means the model guessed. Downgrade rather than trust it.
